correctness.rationale: For any center subset of size \(m\) in a field of order \(q\), the identity \(\sum_x X_A(x)^2=m(q-m)\) follows from quadratic-character orthogonality. The Boolean incidence correction at zero difference yields both children of size at least \((m-\sqrt m-1)/2\). The explicit real thresholds \(T_d=8\cdot2^d-7\cdot2^{d/2}\) satisfy \(T_0=1\) and \(T_d-\sqrt{T_d}-1\ge2T_{d-1}\); induction produces complete adaptive trees. The upper bound requires \(2^d\) distinct terminal hypotheses among at most \(q\) translations. Fresh finite checks corroborate prime and extension-field cases; no extrapolation from computation is used.

value.rationale: For a canonical dense finite-field incidence class, establishes adaptive tree depth within a uniform additive constant of the maximum log_2(q), as opposed to merely a proportional lower bound inherited from known VC estimates. A structural second-moment balancing lemma applies to every adversarially reached version space, giving a genuinely online extension of the analytic finite-field program. The exact invariant is motivated by the 2022 paper’s emphasis on Paley pseudorandom learning complexity; the result does not claim to resolve its static VC conjecture.
